WHILE density is regular they SHALL take the regular value of every token of the density axis this spec names (comp.combobox.option.height.regular, comp.combobox.option.padding-block.regular, comp.combobox.option.padding-inline.regular, comp.combobox.option.gap.regular, comp.combobox.option.leading-icon.size.regular, comp.combobox.option.mark.size.regular, comp.combobox.group-title.padding-inline.regular); WHILE density is compact they SHALL take the compact value of each in its place (comp.combobox.option.height.compact, comp.combobox.option.padding-block.compact, comp.combobox.option.padding-inline.compact, comp.combobox.option.gap.compact, comp.combobox.option.leading-icon.size.compact, comp.combobox.option.mark.size.compact, comp.combobox.group-title.padding-inline.compact), so that a compact option is lower, set in less from its edges and draws smaller glyphs, the room kept for an empty leading icon column (CMB-67) shrinking with them. The text styles, the list's surface and its paddings, the dividers, the group gap and the status row SHALL be the same in both, and so SHALL the field's box. WHEN density names a value the active design system does not have THE combobox SHALL draw the default density's rows and in debug builds report the unknown value; a density a design system added SHALL be drawn from that density's tokens, as the core values are. WHEN density changes while the list is open THE combobox SHALL draw the new rows at once, without a motion, keeping the active option.
behavior.verify: Fixture density-compact under the default system: with a mouse every option is 32 high, its glyphs 20, its content 8 from the row's edges; under touch emulation every option is 48. The field is as high as the regular one's.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform has ARIA attributes (the web), WHEN the product sets an aria- attribute on the host, by the attribute or by the ARIA property that reflects it, THE combobox SHALL move it to the data-aria- attribute of the same name, so that the host is no second node with its name, description or state, and SHALL expose it on the element that carries its role — an id reference by the elements it names in the host's tree or a tree around it, an error message as part of the description while the combobox is invalid — except those the combobox owns (aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-disabled), which it SHALL move and not expose. WHEN the product removes the aria- attribute or its data-aria- twin, or sets the ARIA property that reflects it (ariaLabel, ariaDescribedByElements…) to null, THE combobox SHALL take it off that element. WHEN the product sets an aria- attribute the combobox owns THE combobox SHALL report it in debug builds.

WHILE selection is multiple THE combobox SHALL hold values — the chosen values in the order they were chosen, no two the same — in place of value, which it SHALL keep as it is and ignore, and its input SHALL hold only the text the person types to find an option: it SHALL never write a chosen option's label into it, SHALL draw no chosen option's own glyph at its start (CMB-18), and the committed text it restores (CMB-17) SHALL be the empty text. WHILE selection is single THE combobox SHALL ignore values. WHEN the product changes selection THE combobox SHALL keep value and values as they are, emit nothing, and from then on show the one the new selection names.
behavior.verify: Unit: a multiple combobox given value "lisbon" and values Kyoto and Tokyo draws two entries, Kyoto and Tokyo, and an empty input; switched to single it shows Lisbon and no entry, and back to multiple the two entries again, with no change event.

behavior.text: WHEN the person presses an option that is not disabled by pointer or touch, or presses Enter while such an option is active and no input method is composing, WHILE selection is multiple THE combobox SHALL add the option's value at the end of values WHILE values does not hold it, and take it out of values WHILE it does; it SHALL then empty the text without emitting input, show every option again, keep the list open with that option still the active one, keep focus in the input, emit change once with the new values and announce the change (CMB-79). Such an Enter SHALL do nothing else: it SHALL NOT emit action and SHALL NOT submit a form. The list stays open so that several values can be chosen in a row; it closes by Escape, by the chevron, by a press outside or by leaving (CMB-30, CMB-73).
behavior.verify: Unit, on the web: a press on Kyoto, then Down Arrow to Lisbon and Enter: values Kyoto, Lisbon; two change events, no toggle and no input event; the list stays open and expanded, Lisbon stays active, the input keeps focus and is empty. A press on Kyoto again takes it out. A typed "to" and Enter on its first match empties the text and shows every option.

behavior.text: WHEN the person presses Enter while selection is multiple, no option is active and no input method is composing THE combobox SHALL resolve the text without the white space at its ends. An empty text SHALL commit nothing, and THE combobox SHALL emit action and request the form's submission as CMB-28 says. A text equal to the whole label of an option that is not disabled, compared as CMB-29 compares, SHALL add that option's value as CMB-71 does WHILE values does not hold it, and only empty the text WHILE it does. Any other text SHALL, WHILE allowCustomValue is true, be added at the end of values as it is written, without its white space at both ends, WHILE values does not hold the same text, and the text SHALL be emptied either way; WHILE allowCustomValue is false it SHALL be kept, and the list kept or opened showing what matches or the empty text (CMB-32). An Enter on a text that is not empty SHALL NOT emit action and SHALL NOT submit a form.
behavior.verify: Unit: allowCustomValue true, text " Recursive ", Enter: values ends with "Recursive", one change, no action, the text empty; the same text again adds nothing. allowCustomValue false, text "zzz", Enter: values unchanged, no change, no action, the list shows emptyText. Text "tokyo" with nothing active (no-wrap, Up Arrow to the text) adds Tokyo. An empty text, Enter: action, and in a form one submit.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is multiple: WHEN focus leaves the combobox — its input, its entries and its clear button — for another part of the product THE combobox SHALL close its list with the reason tab or focus-out (CMB-29), choose nothing — neither the active option nor what was typed — and empty the text without emitting input; WHEN the person presses Escape while the list is open THE combobox SHALL close it as CMB-30 says, keeping the text; WHEN they press Escape while the list is closed and the text is not empty it SHALL empty the text, emit input once and stop the key. Leaving and Escape SHALL never remove a chosen value. A choice is a deliberate act in a list of several: leaving the field is not one.
behavior.verify: Unit: values Kyoto, text "lis" with Lisbon active, Tab: the list closes with the reason tab, values is still Kyoto, the text is empty, no change and no input. Text "lis", Escape: the list closes and the text stays; Escape again: the text is empty and one input fires; a third Escape passes on.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is multiple and values is not empty THE combobox SHALL draw each value as a Chip of kind input, size small and the Chip's default variant, in the order of values, inside its container between the leading glyph and the clear button and the chevron, before the input: its label SHALL be the label of the first option whose value it is, or the value itself where it names none, and its remove action SHALL be named by removeLabel with the place {entry} filled by that label. The entries and the input SHALL stand in lines from the start edge, each entry comp.combobox.entries.gap after the one before, a line comp.combobox.entries.row-gap below the one above, every item centred on its line, an entry that does not fit going whole to the next line and none wider than a line, cut as the Chip says; the input SHALL follow the last entry on its line WHILE at least comp.combobox.entries.typing-min-width is left there and start the next line otherwise. THE combobox SHALL show every entry: it SHALL NOT hide one, stand a count in the place of some, scroll its lines or limit its height. The first line SHALL stand where the input line of a combobox with no entry stands, the container SHALL grow by whole lines from the height of its size, the leading glyph, the clear button and the chevron SHALL stay centred on it, and the list SHALL stay anchored below it as it grows (CMB-22).
behavior.verify: Fixtures multiple-values, multiple-open, multiple-many and multiple-outlined. Unit: the distance between two entries on a line and between two lines are comp.combobox.entries.gap and row-gap; with one entry the container is as high as its size; with twelve values at 280 wide it is taller by whole lines, every entry is drawn and the open list starts below the container; the input is never narrower than typing-min-width.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is multiple THE combobox SHALL be one stop in the focus order — its input — and every entry's Chip SHALL be out of the Tab order and stay focusable by the keys, by pointer and by assistive technology. WHEN the person presses Backspace, or the arrow that points to where the line starts, in the input with the caret at the start of the text and nothing selected, and the key is not a repeat of a held key, THE combobox SHALL move focus to the last entry and remove nothing. On an entry: the arrow that points along the line SHALL move focus to the next or the previous entry, past the last to the input with its caret at the start; Home and End SHALL move it to the first and the last entry; Up and Down Arrow SHALL do nothing; Escape and Tab SHALL move it to the input, and Shift+Tab SHALL leave backward as the platform has it; a printable character SHALL move it to the input, where it is typed. WHEN the person presses Backspace or Delete on an entry, or activates its remove action, THE combobox SHALL take that value out of values, emit change once with the new values and announce the removal (CMB-79), having moved focus first — after Backspace to the entry before, or to the one after where it was the first; after Delete or the remove action to the entry after — and to the input where there is none. WHEN the person activates an entry's Chip itself THE combobox SHALL move focus to the input and open its list with that entry's option active where it is shown, removing nothing. These are the chip field's keys (CHF-11 to CHF-14), so that a person who uses both meets the same keys.
behavior.verify: Unit: values Kyoto, Lisbon, Tokyo; Backspace in the empty input focuses Tokyo and removes nothing; Left Arrow focuses Lisbon; Backspace removes Lisbon and focuses Kyoto; Delete on Kyoto removes it and focuses Tokyo; the remove action of Tokyo removes it and focus is in the input. Right Arrow past the last entry returns to the input. In right-to-left, Right Arrow from the input focuses the last entry. A held Backspace that empties the text never reaches an entry. Pressing an entry opens the list with its option active.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is multiple THE combobox SHALL draw every shown option whose value values holds as the chosen one is drawn (CMB-36) — the fill and the check — and expose it as selected and every other option as not selected, and SHALL expose its list as a listbox in which several options can be selected. A list opened by an arrow key or the chevron SHALL have the first shown option whose value values holds active, or the first that is not disabled where it holds none.
behavior.verify: Fixture multiple-open. Unit, on the web: the listbox has aria-multiselectable true; with values Kyoto and Tokyo both rows have aria-selected true and draw the check, the others false; Down Arrow opens the list on Kyoto. The listbox pattern of the APG for several selected options: aria-multiselectable on the listbox and aria-selected on each option, the state every other Tanrei list uses.

behavior.text: WHEN the product sets values THE combobox SHALL draw exactly those entries in that order, a repeated value once, mark the options they name WHILE the list is open, and SHALL NOT emit change or input or announce anything; a value that names no option SHALL be drawn with the value as its label whatever allowCustomValue is. WHILE selection is multiple and clearable is true THE combobox SHALL draw its clear button (CMB-20) WHILE the text or values is not empty and it is neither disabled nor read-only; WHEN it is activated THE combobox SHALL empty the text and values, emit input once with the empty text and change once with the empty values WHILE values was not empty, announce nothing, move focus to the input and leave its list as it is.
behavior.verify: Unit: values set to Tokyo, Tokyo, Kyoto draws Tokyo and Kyoto with no event; a value "atlantis" draws its own text. Clearable with values Kyoto and Tokyo: the clear button is drawn with an empty text; activated, values is empty, one input, one change with the empty values, focus in the input.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform has forms that collect named values (the web's form) and WHILE selection is multiple THE combobox SHALL take part in one as a native select that allows several values does: it SHALL submit one entry for each value, in the order of values, each under its name, none WHILE values is empty, and never the typed text; it SHALL reset to the values it was first given, restore them on navigation, and report a missing value WHILE the Field that frames it says it is required and values is empty, whatever text is typed (CMB-59).
behavior.verify: Unit, on the web: in a form, values Kyoto and Tokyo under the name city: the form data holds city twice, kyoto then tokyo; with values empty it holds no city; a typed "lis" is never sent. A reset returns to the values attribute. In a required Field with values empty and a typed text the combobox is valueMissing; with one value it is valid.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is multiple and values is not empty THE combobox SHALL expose its entries, before its input, as one list named by the combobox's accessible name, each entry an item that holds its Chip — a button named by the entry's label — and that Chip's remove action, named by removeLabel. THE combobox SHALL hold one polite live region of its own, empty at rest and not drawn: WHEN the person adds a value it SHALL put addedText into it with the place {entry} filled by the value's label, and WHEN the person removes one, removedText likewise, the label put in as text of its own direction isolated from the sentence; a later sentence SHALL replace what the region holds. It SHALL announce nothing when the product sets values or when the clear button empties them. THE combobox SHALL take removeLabel, addedText and removedText from the instance's prop and, WHILE that is empty, from the product's words under entryRemoveLabel, entryAddedText and entryRemovedText — the chip field's keys, so that a product writes them once for both — and from nowhere else. WHILE neither gives removeLabel every remove action SHALL still be drawn and work, and debug builds SHALL report that it has no name; WHILE neither gives addedText or removedText nothing SHALL be said, and debug builds SHALL report it.
behavior.verify: Unit: the entries are a list named City with one item for each value, each holding a button named by the label and a remove button named "Remove Kyoto"; with values empty there is no list. Choosing Lisbon puts "Lisbon added" in the live region, removing it "Lisbon removed"; setting values says nothing. Without removeLabel and no words the remove action works and the report names removeLabel; with the product's words set an instance without the props uses them. axe finds no violation in multiple-values, multiple-open, multiple-read-only and multiple-rtl.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is multiple and values is not empty THE combobox SHALL show no placeholder, so that a hint for the first choice does not stand after the last, and SHALL treat itself as not empty for its label, so that a filled or an outlined combobox floats it (CMB-8).
behavior.verify: Fixture multiple-outlined: the label floats over two entries. Unit: a placeholder is shown with values empty and not with one value.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is multiple and the combobox is disabled (CMB-46) THE combobox SHALL draw every entry as a disabled Chip, which takes no focus and cannot be removed, still drawn and exposed. WHILE it is read-only (CMB-47) and not disabled THE combobox SHALL draw every entry as an input Chip without a remove action, reached by the keys of CMB-75, which then remove nothing, and SHALL submit values.
behavior.verify: Fixtures multiple-disabled and multiple-read-only. Unit: read-only, Backspace in the input focuses the last entry, Backspace and Delete there remove nothing and no remove action is drawn; disabled, no entry takes focus and the form data holds no value.

behavior.text: WHERE the layout direction is right-to-left THE combobox SHALL lay its entries out from the right: every line starts at the right edge, the input follows the last entry to its left, and the order of values, of focus and of reading stays the order the values were chosen in; the arrow keys of CMB-75 move the way they point. WHILE the text size is enlarged the entries SHALL grow with it, every one still shown, each on a line of its own where two no longer fit, and the input SHALL stay at least comp.combobox.entries.typing-min-width wide.
behavior.verify: Fixture multiple-rtl. Unit, in right-to-left: the first entry stands at the container's right, before the second; Right Arrow from the empty input focuses the last entry, and Left Arrow past it returns to the input.

accessibility.role: combobox; while selection is multiple, after a list of the chosen values, and its listbox allows several selected options

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the input and on from it; the clear button, while shown, is the next stop. Leaving resolves the text (a typed label chooses its option, any other text is kept as the value or given up) and closes the list; the active option is not chosen.
Edits the text and opens the list, filtered. With allowCustomValue false the first match becomes the active option, read out once typing pauses for half a second; with it true none does.

keyboard.keys: Down Arrow / Up Arrow (also with Alt), list closed
keyboard.action: Opens the list with every option; the chosen option is active, or the first enabled one.

keyboard.keys: Down Arrow / Up Arrow, list open
keyboard.action: Makes the next or previous option active, across groups, and goes round at the ends — Down on the last to the first, Up on the first to the last — unless wrap is false, which stops them. With allowCustomValue true the text is the place before the first option: Up Arrow on the first returns to it with no option active, so that Enter keeps what was typed.

keyboard.keys: Page Down / Page Up, list open
keyboard.action: Moves the active option by ten, stopping at the ends.

keyboard.keys: Home, End, Left Arrow, Right Arrow
keyboard.action: Move the caret in the text, list open or closed.
Chooses it, emits change if the value changed, and closes the list. On a disabled option, nothing. It does not submit a form.

Commits the text: a typed label chooses its option; with allowCustomValue true any other text becomes the value. Then emits action and submits the enclosing form on the web. With allowCustomValue false a text that names no option is not committed and the list stays.

With the list open: closes it, choosing nothing and keeping the text. With the list closed and the text edited: restores the committed value's text. Otherwise the combobox does not act on it. It never clears a committed value.

keyboard.keys: Enter or Space on the clear button
keyboard.action: Empties the text and the value and returns focus to the input.

keyboard.keys: Enter, an option active, selection multiple
keyboard.action: Chooses it, or takes it out where it is chosen; the text empties and the list stays open with the option active. It does not submit a form.

keyboard.keys: Enter, no option active, selection multiple

accessibility.labeling: The accessible name is the label of the Field that frames the combobox, or its own label where no Field does; a filled or outlined combobox draws that name floating, and labelHidden only stops the drawing. The placeholder is never the name. The description is what the Field gives: its supporting text with, in error, the error text after it and its optional text. The combobox is exposed as invalid while error is true or its Field is in error, as required while its Field says so — whichever mark is drawn — and as read-only while readOnly is true. It is expanded while its list is open, and names its active option. Its name also names the list and the chevron's button. An option is named by its label and described by its supporting text, and exposes whether it is the chosen one, whether it is disabled, and its position among the options shown; a group is named by its title. The clear button is named by clearLabel. The status row is a live region. The leading glyphs, the check and the dividers are decorative.
notes: The pattern is the WAI-ARIA editable combobox with a listbox popup: focus stays in the input and the active option is its active descendant on the web, as the search's suggestions are (SRC-14) and a select's options. The input keeps its name, its description, its invalid and required states and its focused edge while the person reads the options, and typing never stops editing the text.

Text entry happens in the platform's native text element: on the web an <input type="text" role="combobox"> in the shadow root with the label, the description and the states set on that element — not through ElementInternals, which axe cannot see.

While an input method composes, every key is the input method's (CMB-16): the Enter that confirms a conversion chooses nothing and submits nothing. A combobox that chose on that Enter cannot be used in Japanese, Chinese or Korean.

With allowCustomValue false, typing makes the first match active, so that Enter chooses what was found; a screen reader reads that option once typing pauses for half a second, not after every key. With allowCustomValue true nothing is active until an arrow key is pressed, so that Enter keeps what was typed, and the text is a stop of the arrow keys between the last option and the first. One rule in both: Enter commits what the field shows as about to be committed. The arrow keys go round at the ends unless wrap is false.
Leaving the field never chooses the active option (CMB-29): a pointer that rested on a row, or the first match of half a word, is not an answer. A whole label typed out is.
Escape closes, then restores, and never clears (CMB-30). Clearing is emptying the text, or the clear button.
The list does not open on focus (CMB-21): tabbing through a form would open a list over the next fields at every stop, and on a touch screen a list would rise together with the keyboard.

Errors are words: a text that names no option is given up, not kept as an error of the combobox's own, and the combobox reports no refusal to its Field (CMB-61); a product that wants to say "choose one from the list" sets error and errorText on the Field, or on the combobox field, from its change and input handlers.
A match is marked by weight (CMB-38), never by color alone and never announced: the label is read whole.
The chevron is a button for a pointer and for touch exploration, outside the focus order; the keyboard opens the list with Down Arrow.
Heights are minimums: at 200% text size the field grows, labels, options and titles wrap, and the list scrolls; only the text in the input stays on one line, and scrolls.
Web: a touch browser zooms the page into an input whose text is smaller than 16 px. Both sizes use 16 px text (comp.input-box.input.typescale.medium).

The combobox draws no frame: the label row, the requirement, the supporting row and the error are those of the Field that frames it (FLD-2 to FLD-13), and the combobox field is that pair as one component. A bare combobox is for a place whose label stands elsewhere — a toolbar, a table cell, a row of an editor — and is named by its own label. The list is an anchored surface by Popover's rules (POP-2 to POP-8, POP-18 to POP-27, POP-34, POP-36, POP-43) with the menu's look; it is not a Popover element, because its content is rows with one meaning, not content of any kind.
How a state looks is a value decision of the active design system; components read the state's tokens and never compute the effect themselves.

The box is the combobox's own part, not a Text input placed in it: the native text element is itself the combobox — it carries the role, the expanded state and the relations to the list and to the active option, which must stand in one tree with it — and the keys, the text a choice writes and the commit are the combobox's. Its drawing is the box every input control is drawn on, from the one set of tokens `comp.input-box` that the text input, the select, the number input and the color input read too (CMB-63): the two are one drawing, and neither is built from the other.

WCAG 2.5.8 (target size): for touch every option is at least the touch target high in both densities (CMB-34). The compact density is lower than the pointer target for a fine pointer, by design: it is the density of a tool used with a mouse, it stays above the 24 by 24 the criterion asks, and its options reach across the list's whole width. A product that cannot accept that uses regular.

Several values (selection multiple) follow the APG combobox with a listbox that allows several selected options: aria-multiselectable on the listbox and aria-selected on each option, as every other Tanrei list says selection. The chosen values stand before the input as input Chips in a list named by the combobox's name, each with a remove action named in the product's words, and a live region says what was added or removed.

While selection is multiple the list stays open after a choice, so that several values can be chosen in a row, and the typed text empties, so that the next search starts from nothing: as Ant Design's Select in mode multiple, Carbon's multiselect and Mantine's MultiSelect do (MUI's Autocomplete closes unless disableCloseOnSelect is set). Leaving chooses nothing and empties the text, as MUI's Autocomplete and Ant Design's Select clear the search on blur: a value is added only by a choice.

Backspace on an empty input moves focus to the last chosen value and removes nothing; a second Backspace removes it. MUI, Ant Design and Mantine remove the last value at once; Tanrei follows its own chip field (CHF-12), so that the two fields of one product answer the same key the same way and a value is never removed by a key whose effect was not seen first: the focused chip is read out before it can be removed.

web.notes: Lagging: the element in the repository still draws its own label row, requirement mark and supporting row and has the ten props of a frame; the bare control without them is not built on this platform yet. As specified: `tanrei-combobox`, class `TanreiCombobox`, React `Combobox`. A form-associated custom element (`static formAssociated = true`): it takes `name`, submits `value` (never the uncommitted text), restores it on navigation, resets to the `value` attribute, follows `<fieldset disabled>` and reports `valueMissing` while its Field says it is required (CMB-59); its two calls on `ElementInternals` and its form for Enter go through the shared composing primitives, so that a composed element that holds it can be the form's control in its place. The options are `<tanrei-option>` and `<tanrei-option-group>` children, observed for changes; the combobox reads them and renders the rows itself in its shadow root, so that the `<input role="combobox">`, its `aria-controls` listbox and its `aria-activedescendant` option are in one tree. **Options through a slot**: a `<slot>` element among its children stands for the elements assigned to it, flattened (`assignedElements({ flatten: true })`), in the slot's place among the other children; the combobox reads them as its own options, reads again on that slot's `slotchange`, and observes each assigned element as it observes a child. This is `readOptions()` and `OptionsController` in `primitives/option-list.ts`, shared with the select, and it is how a composed element gives the combobox the product's options without moving or copying an element. The input carries `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"` and `aria-readonly`, with `autocomplete="off"`, `autocapitalize="none"` and `spellcheck="false"`; its name, its description and its invalid and required states are values — its own `label`, or what the Field's connection gives (`packages/web/src/primitives/field.ts`) — written on the input as `aria-label`, `aria-description`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required`, because an id cannot be referenced across a shadow root. To that connection the combobox says that it draws the label (a filled or outlined variant) and its inset (CMB-61), and takes from it `labelHidden` and the required mark besides. Composition is read from `compositionstart` / `compositionend` and `event.isComposing` (and `keyCode 229`), and keys are ignored while it lasts. The chevron is a `<button tabindex="-1" aria-label aria-expanded>` and the clear button a `<tanrei-button variant="text" size="small">`; `pointerdown` on a row, the chevron or the list calls `preventDefault` so that focus stays in the input. The list is a manual popover in the top layer, placed with CSS anchor positioning and a script fallback, sized to the anchor's width and followed with the `FollowController` the menu uses, with the combobox's own light dismiss so that `toggle` carries a reason; the element itself is the opener, so a press on the label row of a Field around it is a press outside (CMB-30). On a touch device `visualViewport` gives the keyboard's edge. The match is a `<mark>` with `background: none` and a heavier `font-weight`, inside the option's one text node sequence, which assistive technology reads as one label. `input` is the native composed event (the text is `inputValue`); the combobox sets its own `value` before firing `change` (a composed, bubbling CustomEvent whose `detail` holds `value` and `inputValue`) and its own `open` before firing `toggle` (`detail` holds `open` and `reason`), a CustomEvent that is composed and does not bubble, as the platform's own `toggle` does not. The element in the repository fires a `toggle` that is neither yet, and an event that is not composed never leaves the shadow root of an element that holds the combobox. Attributes are kebab-case (`input-value`, `label-hidden`, `allow-custom-value`, `clear-label`, `status-text`, `empty-text`) except `readonly`; a boolean attribute cannot default to true, so the web names the inverse of chevron: `no-chevron`, and of wrap: `no-wrap` (the `wrap` property stays). An option typing made active is named by `aria-activedescendant` 500 ms after it became active, from a timer each change of the text restarts. The `leading-icon` slot is a named slot. The `inline` attribute draws an open list in place under the box, for the fixtures. Parts: `container`, `outline`, `active-indicator`, `label` and `requirement-label` (the floating label and its asterisk), `input`, `leading-icon`, `clear-button`, `chevron`, `list`, `option`, `option-label`, `option-supporting-text`, `option-leading-icon`, `mark`, `group`, `group-title`, `divider`, `status`. Before the element is defined its options are running text: a page hides them with `tanrei-combobox:not(:defined) > * { display: none }` and gives the tag a block size. A `<datalist>` is not used: its list takes no token, no supporting text, no group and no status, and browsers disagree on how it filters. Words: the element has no words of its own. `empty-text` and `clear-label` left empty read the product's words, set once with `setWords()` from `@tanrei/web`; the element draws again when they change. **Several values**: `selection="multiple"` with `values` — a property that takes an array, and an attribute read as a JSON array or as words (`values='["kyoto","tokyo"]'`, `values="kyoto tokyo"`) that is also what a form reset returns to. Each value is a `<tanrei-chip kind="input" size="small" tabindex="-1">` in a `role="list"` element in the container, before the input; the chips' parts leave under `entry-container`, `entry-label` and `entry-remove`, and the chip itself is the part `entry`. The listbox carries `aria-multiselectable="true"`. The form value is a `FormData` with one entry per value under `name`. `change`'s `detail` then holds `values` (the new array) beside `value` and `inputValue`. A hidden `aria-live="polite"` region says what was added or removed.
